name: Champagne
summary: Champagne, a dominant dilution caused by one missense change in SLC36A1 on chromosome 14 (c.188C>G, T63R). It lightens both pigments: red to gold and black to brown or chocolate - gold champagne on a chestnut, amber on a bay, classic on a black. One copy and two look the same; no visible double-champagne effect is established. Its surest signs are in the skin and eyes rather than the coat: pinkish or lavender skin that gains darker mottling with age, and eyes that are blue or blue-green in the foal and darken to amber, hazel or light brown. UC Davis recognises one champagne allele only. Described as concentrated in the Tennessee Walking Horse, Missouri Fox Trotter, American Cream Draft, Quarter Horse and related breeds, without published figures.

phenotypes.name: Champagne
phenotypes.description: Both pigments diluted: red to gold and black to brown or chocolate - gold champagne on a chestnut, amber champagne with brown points on a bay, classic champagne, a dark tan or taupe, on a black. One copy and two look the same. The skin is pinkish or lavender and mottles darker with age; the eyes are blue or blue-green in the foal and darken to amber, hazel or light brown.
